title: Zang International with Lynette Zang: Farmers Get 11.8¢ of Each Domestic Food Dollar—Where
description:
Original video author: Zang International with Lynette Zang. Independent recap and commentary; no endorsement implied. Farmers receive 11.8 cents of each dollar spent on domestically produced food, according to the USDA figure cited by Zang International with Lynette Zang. This recap explains the channel’s breakdown: 11.8 cents reaches the farm, while 88.2 cents goes to the marketing share, including processing, transportation, storage, wholesaling and retailing. Our take acknowledges the stress of grocery spending while noting that this split alone doesn’t establish unfair pricing or profit margins. Credit: Zang International with Lynette Zang.

For entertainment and informational purposes only. This is not financial, legal, medical, or other professional advice. Consult a qualified professional about your circumstances. We are not responsible for decisions or results based on this video.

hook: Just 11.8 cents of your domestic food dollar reaches the farm, in the USDA’s 2024 estimate.
reporter_prompt: Horizontal documentary opening inside an American supermarket produce department. A middle-aged American male reporter in a blue polo stands beside bins of domestically grown produce, with shoppers and grocery shelves visible behind him. Natural soft overhead lighting, warm curiosity, measured conversational delivery. Use real location footage, not a studio or green screen.
